blurb: The long-haired Siamese: pointed coat, sapphire-blue eyes and a plumed tail
description: The Balinese is a long-haired Siamese-type cat with Thai roots: slender, with a silky medium coat, pointed coloring, blue eyes and a sociable, vocal nature.
answer: The Balinese is a long-haired cat breed that arose as a natural mutation of the Siamese, whose ancestors came from Thailand, and was developed as a breed in the United States from the 1950s. It is a slender, graceful cat with a silky medium-length coat, Siamese-style points and blue eyes, and is described as sociable, vocal and playful.

body: Some of the first Siamese imported from Thailand to the US and UK in the mid-1800s carried a recessive long-hair gene. Long-haired kittens were at first treated as a fault and sold as pets, but 'Long-haired Siamese' were registered as show cats in 1928, and in the mid-1950s US breeders began developing them as a separate breed. Breeder Helen Smith named it Balinese after the grace of Balinese dancers; the cats have no connection with Bali.

Breeder Sylvia Holland helped set the standard in the 1960s and 1970s. Long-haired cats in other point colors were classed as the Javanese, and in 2008 the CFA's breed councils made the Javanese a color division of the Balinese. Like the Siamese, the breed split into a traditional type and a slender modern type.

Both types are slender, fine-boned cats with long legs and tails, oval paws, almond-shaped eyes and large pointed ears. The traditional type is sturdier with a broader head; the modern type has a pronounced wedge-shaped head, long muzzle and more elongated body.

The coat is medium-length, soft and silky, without a fluffy undercoat, and the tail carries a definite plume. Kittens are born cream or white and develop points on the face, ears, paws and tail, a heat-sensitive form of partial albinism. Eyes range from pale blue to sapphire or violet. Most associations accept seal, blue, chocolate, lilac, red and cream points plus tortoiseshell and lynx; the CFA classes colors beyond the classic four as the Javanese division.

As commonly described, Balinese share the Siamese personality: social, playful, inquisitive and intelligent, with a strong interest in what goes on around them. They are often vocal, though reportedly quieter than the Siamese, and are described as clingy, energetic, acrobatic and sometimes dog-like, so they may need a lot of attention.

Because the silky coat lacks a thick undercoat, it is generally described as easier to maintain than many long-haired coats, though occasional brushing helps. Their high energy and need for attention suggest daily play and company are important.

The breed developed from a small gene pool, which may raise the chance of inherited disorders. Conditions reported in the breed include progressive retinal atrophy (PRA), a degeneration of the retina that may impair vision. Breed clubs recommend health screening of breeding stock.

faq.q: Is a Balinese cat just a long-haired Siamese?
faq.a: Essentially yes. It originated as a natural long-hair mutation of the Siamese and is the same type of cat with a medium-length silky coat and a plumed tail.

faq.q: Do Balinese cats meow a lot?
faq.a: They are commonly described as vocal and persistent talkers, though usually at a lower volume than the Siamese.
